_comment: Canonical-claim manifest for check-claims.js (#300). Each entry pins a rule that MUST keep being stated by every file listed, because #294 proved that a correct claim fixed in one file routinely goes stale, narrowed or absent in the others. Read check-claims.js's header before trusting a green run: this guard confirms a claim TRAVELLED, never that it is TRUE, and it cannot see a fix that says more than intended. Patterns are JS regex sources matched case-insensitively against the file with whitespace collapsed and markdown emphasis markers stripped, so one entry spans the wording variants a claim legitimately has. Consumer lists were derived by measuring the current tree, not by assumption — the issue that proposed this guard listed phrases that did not exist verbatim anywhere.

claims.why: A clean Codex rerun can arrive as a 👍 reaction or as an INLINE REVIEW-THREAD REPLY, and an inline reply never enters the comment list. A file that says only 'check the comments' sends a session to a gate it cannot clear. Round 35 of #294 found the narrowed form in nine files while the source said both.

Codex-authored and naming the current head proves the run happened, not that it was clean — a review WITH live findings names the head too. Round 36 of #294 fixed the inverted form, which had authorised merging over open findings. The claim travels in two shapes (a response is not a verdict; a reaction is not a verdict) and the pattern accepts both, because both are the same rule about what clears the gate.

ci-notify resolves ONE open PR from a head SHA, else branch plus head-repo owner, and exits silently otherwise — and a repository_dispatch run's default-branch SHA can uniquely match an unrelated promotion PR, which gets the comment instead. A unique match is therefore not proof that YOUR session will be woken, and any file that implies otherwise sends a session to wait on a signal that will not arrive.

The counterpart to the wake gap above: when a run could end without waking the session, the check-in is what keeps the PR from being abandoned mid-flight. Rounds 37 and 39 of #294 were both this claim failing to reach a consumer — round 39's was in a shell script whose PreToolUse message is the highest-authority copy of the rule, and every .md-only sweep missed it. Consumers here deliberately include both .yml carriers for the same reason.
